content.tagline: A dirty panel loses up to two thirds of its output. A robot brings it back
content.descriptor: Chinese maker of robots and brushes for solar panel cleaning; own plant, national high-tech enterprise status
about: BeiJing Multifit Electrical Technology Co., Ltd. manufactures cleaning equipment for solar panels. Headquarters in Beijing, plant in Shantou (Guangdong), branches in Shenzhen and Sichuan. The company holds national high-tech enterprise status and trades under the MULTIFIT name.

The problem this equipment solves is measured in money. Dust, bird droppings and rust particles cut a panel's output to 20–36% of nominal; after cleaning, efficiency returns to 90–95% and falls again if maintenance stops. Beyond lost output, soiling is physically dangerous: a shaded section overheats, hot spots form, the panel degrades and can burn out. Cleaning is therefore not cosmetic — it extends the life of the plant.

The range splits in two. Robots: the MR-G series for single and double panel rows, the MR-T1 and MR-T2 series, and the MR-AR transport trolley that moves a robot between rows. MULR brushes — from hand models to a water-driven version — cover the places where a robot is overkill. For every model the company provides a performance calculation: cleaning area per hour, daily rate, and the time needed for an array of a given size.

lines.name: MR-G — robots for panel rows
lines.note: The core series, in single-row and double-row versions. Travel speed around 12 m/min; throughput and daily rate are calculated for the specific array.

lines.name: MR-T1 / MR-T2
lines.note: Robot series for other plant configurations, differing in working width and operating mode; chosen by the geometry of the array.

lines.name: MR-AR — transport trolley
lines.note: Carries a robot between panel rows and removes the manual repositioning step. Needed where rows are many and set apart.

lines.name: MULR — cleaning brushes
lines.note: A brush range from hand models to a water-driven version. The answer for spots where a robot is excessive or cannot reach.
